name: Settlement Lock-in
description: Inside the last minute the settlement value is a 60-second average that is partly already fixed. If traders price off current spot vs strike, a model of the partly locked-in average should beat the market, especially just after spot crosses the strike.
hypothesis: Inside the settlement window (last 60 s), (60-tau)/60 of the settlement average is fixed; spot-watchers misprice it, especially right after a strike cross. Wrong if a partial-average model loses to the next real fill in log loss, or buying its side at real fills after fees is <= 0 in both halves.
next: Rejected at research: the market beats the partial-average model at every horizon (traders track the CF index); strike-cross cases aren't mispriced; no late favourite-longshot bias; Kalshi trade size carries no tradable information.
